publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Taken together, these and other results are compelling evidence that the hippocampus serves as a center for spatially related behaviors in birds, as in mammals.

span.label: spatial cognition in birds
span.quote: Spatial cognition in birds is an exciting, forming research field which will continue to provide important insights on the evolution and mechanisms of spatial cognition.

span.label: review
span.quote: The aim of this primer is to highlight the insights and questions in the field of spatial cognition in birds, with an emphasis on recent research attempting to close the knowledge gap between birds and mammals by shedding light on the neural mechanisms of spatial cognition in birds.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Species differ in place-cell abundance because the ecological demand for spatial memory differs: caching and homing species that must remember many locations develop robust place coding, species that do not need it show little
span.quote: A hypothesis explaining this diversity is that the occurrence of place cells across species is correlated with strong reliance on spatial memory capacities.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Because caching birds must retrieve many hidden items, selection for that behaviour is what produces the enlarged hippocampus and abundant place cells, so place cells are proposed to serve spatial memory rather than merely accompany it
span.quote: finding robust place cells in a bird that specializes in its food-caching behaviors, and not in a species that does not exhibit such behavior, provides strong support for the hypothesis that place cells contribute to spatial memory.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Head direction tuning in a migratory seabird is anchored by the earth's magnetic field, the cells encoding head angle relative to magnetic north
span.quote: The plausible explanation is that the cells are sensitive to the angle of the head relative to the magnetic north.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Knowing one's own place and heading requires converting head- and body-centred sensory input into an environment-fixed frame, a transformation performed in and upstream of the hippocampus
span.quote: To know one’s own position and direction requires a transformation from egocentric sensory inputs that move with the animal’s head and body to allocentric representations that are fixed in the environment.

span.label: The neural mechanisms of avian spatial cognition remain poorly understood.
span.note: what this limits: any mechanistic claim in the review: OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEURAL MECHANISMS OF SPATIAL COGNITION IN BIRDS IS STILL POOR
span.quote: But our understanding of the neural mechanisms of spatial cognition in birds is still poor.

span.label: All avian hippocampal recordings so far come from small enclosures, unlike the scales at which birds actually navigate.
span.note: what this limits: every avian hippocampal recording in the literature: TO DATE, ALL THE EXPERIMENTS IN WHICH BRAIN ACTIVITY WAS RECORDED IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS OF BIRDS HAVE BEEN CONDUCTED IN RELATIVELY SMALL ENVIRONMENTS - unlike the scales at which birds navigate
span.quote: To date, all the experiments in which brain activity was recorded in the hippocampus of birds have been conducted in relatively small environments (Figure 3A).

span.label: How the earth's magnetic field shapes the avian head-direction system is not yet resolved.
span.note: what this limits: the magnetic-field question specifically: FURTHER EXAMINATION OF HEAD DIRECTION CELLS IN STREAKED SHEARWATER AND OTHER BIRDS IS NECESSARY TO RESOLVE HOW THE HEAD DIRECTION SYSTEM IN THE AVIAN HIPPOCAMPUS IS INFLUENCED BY THE EARTH'S MAGNETIC FIELD
span.quote: Further examination of head direction cells in streaked shearwater and other birds is necessary to resolve how the head direction system in the avian hippocampus is influenced by the earth’s magnetic field.

span.label: The category's criterion comes from another species, and 2% of the units tested meet it.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about place cells in birds: of more than 2,000 single units recorded in quail hippocampus, only about 2% passed the criterion for place cells, and most of those did not show the clear single field expected from the classical place cells found in rodents
span.quote: Extensive analysis of more than 2,000 single units in the hippocampus of quails found little evidence of place cells in quails: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents

span.label: The structure is called a homologue and stated to differ fundamentally in architecture.
span.note: what this limits: any transfer of a mammalian hippocampal result to birds: the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus has an architecture that, after three hundred million years of independent evolution, differs fundamentally from the mammalian one
span.quote: Research on the development, connectivity and cellular markers of avian brains has identified the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus. Three hundred million years of independent evolution have given rise to an hippocampal architecture in birds which differs fundamentally from that of the mammalian hippocampus

span.label: place cells
span.quote: Extensive analysis of more than 2,000 single units in the hippocampus of quails found little evidence of place cells in quails: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents

span.label: avian homologue
span.quote: Research on the development, connectivity and cellular markers of avian brains has identified the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus. Three hundred million years of independent evolution have given rise to an hippocampal architecture in birds which differs fundamentally from that of the mammalian hippocampus

span.label: mammalian hippocampus
span.quote: Research on the development, connectivity and cellular markers of avian brains has identified the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus. Three hundred million years of independent evolution have given rise to an hippocampal architecture in birds which differs fundamentally from that of the mammalian hippocampus

span.label: cognitive maps
span.quote: Unlike the wellstudied cognitive maps in rodents traversing small areas, however, these cognitive maps need to represent, in some species of birds, ranges of hundreds and thousands of kilometers

span.label: criterion
span.quote: Extensive analysis of more than 2,000 single units in the hippocampus of quails found little evidence of place cells in quails: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents

span.label: a place cell - A RODENT-DERIVED CRITERION APPLIED ACROSS A PHYLUM: about 2% of more than 2,000 quail hippocampal units passed the criterion, and most of those lacked the clear single field of activity the classical rodent place cells show, so the category is being tested in birds by a standard defined on the animal it was discovered in
span.quote: Extensive analysis of more than 2,000 single units in the hippocampus of quails found little evidence of place cells in quails: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents

span.label: the avian hippocampus - A HOMOLOGUE THAT DIFFERS FUNDAMENTALLY: identified as the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus by development, connectivity and cellular markers, and stated in the next sentence to have an architecture fundamentally different after three hundred million years of independent evolution - the correspondence and the difference are asserted together
span.quote: Research on the development, connectivity and cellular markers of avian brains has identified the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus. Three hundred million years of independent evolution have given rise to an hippocampal architecture in birds which differs fundamentally from that of the mammalian hippocampus

span.label: a cognitive map - A DIFFERENT ORDER OF MAGNITUDE IN BIRDS: the well-studied rodent maps cover small areas while avian maps must represent ranges of hundreds and thousands of kilometres, so the same term names representations whose spatial scale differs by several orders
span.quote: Unlike the wellstudied cognitive maps in rodents traversing small areas, however, these cognitive maps need to represent, in some species of birds, ranges of hundreds and thousands of kilometers

span.label: builds-on → Edward Tolman, 'Cognitive maps in rats and men'
span.quote: This metaphor, dated to the early days of spatial cognition research, stresses the importance of studying cognitive maps in birds.

span.label: avian homologue —same-as→ mammalian hippocampus
span.note: differs in: hippocampal architecture, after three hundred million years of independent evolution · strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: Research on the development, connectivity and cellular markers of avian brains has identified the avian homologue of the mammalian hippocampus. Three hundred million years of independent evolution have given rise to an hippocampal architecture in birds which differs fundamentally from that of the mammalian hippocampus

span.label: The avian and mammalian hippocampi share an origin but are architecturally different, the avian one being an unfolded surface sheet without a granule layer.
span.quote: For example, the avian hippocampus is a neuronal sheet spreading along the dorsal surface of the caudal medial pallium, while the mammalian hippocampus is a folded structure hidden below the neocortex.

span.label: The avian hippocampus lacks the granule layer that defines the mammalian structure.
span.quote: The avian hippocampus lacks a distinct granule layer, which robustly characterizes the mammalian hippocampus.

span.label: Lesion work establishes the avian hippocampus as necessary for spatial behaviour, including pigeon homing.
span.quote: Furthermore, experiments conducted with homing pigeons have consistently shown that hippocampal-lesioned individuals have impaired homing behaviors.

span.label: Immediate-early gene expression rises in hippocampal neurons of birds searching remembered food locations, a second line of evidence tying the structure to spatial memory.
span.quote: Early gene expression was found to increase in the hippocampal neurons of birds searching for memorized locations of food items in mazes or open arenas, suggesting that the activation of these neurons is necessary for memorizing locations.

span.label: Hippocampus size scales with food-caching specialisation across bird species, and caching chickadees recruit more new neurons in the caching season.
span.quote: In species of birds that specialize in food caching, such as titmice, chickadees and jays, the hippocampus is larger than that of most non-food-caching birds.

span.label: Recordings in Japanese quail found almost no classical place cells but a substantial population of head direction cells.
span.quote: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents.

span.label: Tufted titmice, a food-caching species, yielded the first clear avian place cells, covering the arena as in rodents, while non-caching zebra finches did not.
span.quote: These findings are of twofold importance: they are the first clear evidence for place cells in a bird species

span.label: Place coding was weak in the non-caching zebra finch, giving the contrast that supports the memory-demand account.
span.quote: Place cells were significantly less common and less robust in zebra finches.

span.label: Wireless recordings in flying barn owls showed hippocampal cells with place fields covering the flight space, extending place coding beyond ground locomotion.
span.quote: Preliminary results of these experiments showed that some cells in the hippocampus reliably fired action potentials when the owl flew through a confined field in the flight room.

span.label: Head direction cells in a migratory seabird were biased toward north and kept that bias indoors and outdoors.
span.quote: Head direction cells recorded in these birds mostly pointed to or near north.

span.label: spatial cognition
span.quote: Together these computations mediate the process referred to as spatial cognition, the study of which has been one of the most active research fields in modern neuroscience.

span.label: place cell
span.quote: he found cells that fired action potentials when the rat passed through a specific place in the environment. Examining the activity pattern of such ‘place cells’, he concluded that the hippocampus may contain a ‘cognitive map’ that

span.label: cognitive map
span.quote: Examining the activity pattern of such ‘place cells’, he concluded that the hippocampus may contain a ‘cognitive map’ that represents the animal’s location in its proximate environment.

span.label: head direction cells and grid cells
span.term: head direction cells and grid cells
span.quote: head direction cells, which increase response whenever the head is pointing in a specific direction in the environment; grid cells, which respond when the animal is at regular intervals in the environment;

span.label: border cells
span.quote: border cells, which respond when the animal is near a specific wall in the environment; and more.

span.label: central-place foraging
span.quote: This type of behavior, called central-place foraging, is another demonstration of the remarkable spatial cognition capabilities that have evolved in bird species.

span.label: criterion for a classical place cell (tiling the environment)
span.term: criterion for a classical place cell (tiling the environment)
span.quote: Place cells in rodents robustly and stably represent single locations in the environment, such that the population of place cells tiles the whole environment.

span.label: ~2% — Proportion of recorded quail hippocampal units meeting the place-cell criterion
span.quote: only ~2% of the recorded units passed the criterion for place cells, and even in this small population of cells, most units did not show a clear single field of activity as expected from the classical place cells found in rodents.

span.label: about 12% — Proportion of quail hippocampal cells classified as head direction cells
span.quote: they discovered that about 12% of the cells were ‘head direction’ cells.

span.label: More than 60% — Proportion of recorded tufted titmouse hippocampal cells classified as place cells
span.quote: More than 60% of the recorded cells were classified as place cells, which, together, fully represented the experimental arena, like place cells in rodents

span.label: more than 2,000 — Single units analysed in the quail hippocampus study
span.quote: Extensive analysis of more than 2,000 single units in the hippocampus of quails found little evidence of place cells in quails

span.label: around 300 million years — Time since the bird and mammal lineages diverged, the evolutionary distance that makes the comparison informative
span.quote: From an evolutionary standpoint, birds and mammals diverged around 300 million years ago

span.label: 200-meter-long — Length of the tunnel in which flying bats showed multifocal place fields, the cited evidence that spatial coding changes with environment scale
span.quote: However, bats flying in a 200-meter-long tunnel exhibit place cells with multifocal place fields of varying width.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2022.06.080.
